features.name: any_named_real_world_analogy_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment contain a named, real-world analogy or example (e.g., a specific historical or scientific case)?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment, in its own assertions, uses a named, real-world analogy or example (specific identifiable historical event/person, scientific study/phenomenon, or other concrete named real-world case) to argue against the OP's view. Return 0 if no comment does (valid empty list gives 0). Hypothetical or unnamed generic examples do not count. Quoted material counts only if the commenter adopts it as support. Ignore any OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome as evidence. Malformed/missing input gives null.

features.name: any_abstract_logical_rebuttal_comment
features.definition: Does at least one counter-argument comment make an abstract logical rebuttal without relying on a named real-world analogy or example?
features.spec: Parse OC_comments (JSON list of comments by other users). Return 1 if at least one comment rebuts the OP's view mainly through abstract logical reasoning (e.g., pointing out inconsistencies, definitions, premises, inference flaws) and that comment contains no named real-world analogy or example (specific historical/scientific case). Return 0 otherwise (valid empty list gives 0). Comments may be in both this and the named-analogy feature across different comments in a row; overlap and neither cases are allowed. Ignore OP view-change/delta-award announcements, post-outcome resolution updates or reports of the outcome. Malformed/missing input gives null.

h0: Rows with named real-world analogy comments (any_named_real_world_analogy_comment) have the same view-change rate as rows with abstract logical rebuttal comments (any_abstract_logical_rebuttal_comment).
h1: Rows with named real-world analogy comments have a higher view-change rate than rows with abstract logical rebuttal comments.
note: The claim is a contrast (beta_analogy minus beta_abstract), which neither coefficient in this formula represents alone, so term=null; no difference score is invented. Both sides are measured at row level, overlap and neither cases possible. Comparison is of presence, since no count/share was specified. OC_comments may contain outcome announcements; no per-comment outcomes or timing available, so only associations at row level can be described. "Abstract logical rebuttal" operationalized as a comment without a named real-world example.
